trust_decision.summary: Whether a task may change state (terminal states are final; cancel is allowed only from a non-terminal state). At the pinned commit cancel_task checks this on a snapshot read and only later writes, and the store's update() never checks it.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'inmemory.rs update race condition', so an engineer opens InMemoryTaskStore::update first. The cancel check-then-act it pairs with is in a different file, handler.rs.

fix_sites.entry_point: public TaskStore::update; reached via DefaultRequestHandler send_message / send_streaming_message (drive_execution -> apply_event_to_task -> save_task) and cancel_task
public TaskStore trait, used by any third-party store that does not override it

DefaultRequestHandler::cancel_task <- JSON-RPC tasks/cancel (a2a-server/src/jsonrpc.rs:106-109), REST POST /tasks/{id}:cancel and legacy /tasks/{id}/cancel (a2a-server/src/rest.rs:87, 244-282), gRPC CancelTask (a2a-grpc/src/server.rs:129-141), SlimRPC CancelTask (a2a-slimrpc/src/server.rs:73-80)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: a2a-server/src/task_store/store.rs:17-39 (the fix adds trait default begin_cancel at fix.diff:224-237, and the in-memory update terminal guard at fix.diff:90-95 sits in the store impl, not the trait contract at a2a-server/src/task_store/store.rs:22-23)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report points at a cancel race in the handler, so a solver can argue that the store's update() is generic persistence with no state machine of its own, and that the public TaskStore trait with its non-atomic default is the store implementer's job. The fix itself documents its default begin_cancel as non-atomic (fix.diff:221-223).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Re-cancelling an already-CANCELED task must stay idempotent, and once begin_cancel has set CANCELED, the executor's own cancel stream re-emits a CANCELED status/task that save_task must still store (same terminal state, new message). A fix that rejects every update on a terminal task, or treats a raced cancel as an error, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: update to a different terminal state (Completed -> Canceled/Failed)
update from terminal back to non-terminal (Completed -> Submitted/Working)
update re-applying the same terminal state (allowed)
two concurrent cancels on one non-terminal task (both return CANCELED)
cancel racing with completion (raced task terminal but not CANCELED -> TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE)

O7_producer.where: a2a-server/src/handler.rs:226-250 (apply_event_to_task builds the full Task written by save_task from executor events, using a possibly stale current_task copy)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: send_message / send_streaming_message with message.task_id naming a terminal task: prepare_task_for_execution reuses the stored task without checking terminal state, saves a push config for it, and starts an executor on it. The fix's update guard only rejects the executor's later write.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is the send-message feature, not cancel, and the store now rejects the state write anyway, so a solver can call it 'already covered'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the cancel fix site (handler.rs), different function, about 200 lines away; a different file from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An ArtifactUpdate event (or a Task event with the same terminal state) still changes a terminal task's artifacts/history, because the fix's guard compares only status.state.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix deliberately allows re-applying the same terminal state for idempotent re-emission, so a solver reads content changes as legitimate.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: handler.rs mapper vs inmemory.rs guard: 2 files, same crate

O8_uncovered_routes.route: drive_execution checks the in-memory execution snapshot for terminal state and then writes. begin_cancel updates only the store, never the ActiveExecution snapshot, so the snapshot check is a stale check-then-act on the same task.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The store guard now rejects the write and the loop breaks on error, so a solver sees only a subscriber-visible error, not a state change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second in-tree TaskStore (e.g. a file- or sqlite-backed store) whose update() lacks the terminal guard and which inherits the non-atomic default begin_cancel
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TaskStore is a public trait with the comment 'Contents do not survive restarts' on the in-memory one (a2a-server/src/task_store/inmemory.rs:17), so a persistent store is the natural next addition and would be a real second implementation at distance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a delegating wrapper store (like the test PagingTaskStore) that forwards update but not begin_cancel, so it silently falls back to the non-atomic default
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Wrappers that forward only the methods that existed when they were written are common, and the test double already forwards create/update/get/list only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a resume/continue path (InputRequired -> Working) that does get-then-update without an atomic transition, like begin_cancel
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Multi-turn resume is part of A2A, and the existing code already reuses the stored task without a state check.

O9_family: Race / TOCTOU on a task state machine (CWE-362): non-atomic check-then-act on cancel, plus a missing terminal-state immutability check in the store

O10_build.toolchain: cargo (workspace; a2a-pb has build.rs protobuf codegen at a2a-pb/build.rs, with generated code checked in at a2a-pb/src/gen/)
O10_build.project_tests: Unit tests in a2a-server/src/task_store/inmemory.rs (mod tests, update tests about lines 170-195) and a2a-server/src/handler.rs (cancel tests at lines 1745-1850), run with tokio::test

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Take a handler-level mutex around cancel_task, or re-check state right before the write in the handler, and leave store update() and the public trait without any terminal-state guard.

out_of_scope_notes: cancel_task calls execution_manager.finish (a2a-server/src/handler.rs:879-881) while drive_execution may still be running; this concerns lifecycle cleanup, not the terminal-state check.
subscribe_to_task does not return UnsupportedOperation for terminal tasks as a2a-pb/proto/a2a.proto:75 requires (a2a-server/src/handler.rs:886-899); spec conformance, not this race.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell used); the source tree is about 65 .rs files plus checked-in protobuf codegen, so tiny_repo (<5 MB) may apply and was not confirmed.

Whether the concurrent-cancel race can be shown deterministically by a hidden test: tokio::test defaults to a current-thread runtime, so the fix's own concurrency test (fix.diff:38-73) may pass even without the fix; this hurts how well the race half can be tested.
present_in_latest for all O8 routes: no latest release given.
